items.q: Do you supply customers outside the UAE?

items.q: Where can I get the software?

items.q: Can I visit the showroom?

faq.title: Before you choose.
faq.lead: A few things to consider when planning your system.

items.q: How is time attendance different from access control?
items.a: Time attendance records when people check in and out. Access control manages entry to a door or area. Some terminals support both; check the individual model specifications.

items.q: Can I keep my existing software or door hardware?
items.a: Compatibility depends on the model, connections and software version. Share the details of your current system with AIMS before choosing new equipment.

items.q: Can AIMS help with installation?
items.a: AIMS supplies and installs systems in the UAE. Contact the team with your site location, the number of doors or users, and any existing equipment to discuss the scope.

items.q: What if I already know the model I need?
items.a: Use the search in the header to find the model, view its published specifications and add it to your quote list.

items.q: How many attendance terminals do I need?
items.a: Usually one per entrance staff use at shift change. Large teams may need more so queues stay short. AIMS will suggest a number from your headcount and entrances.

items.q: Face, fingerprint or card for time attendance?
items.a: Face is touch-free and fast. Fingerprint has a low cost per person. Cards are familiar but can be lent, so many sites pair them with face or fingerprint.

items.q: Can one attendance system cover several sites?
items.a: Yes. BioTime Cloud, or BioTime on a server your sites can reach, collects punches from terminals in different locations.

items.q: Can attendance terminals also open a door?
items.a: Some models support access control as well as attendance. Check the model's specifications, or ask AIMS about the lock and exit button it needs.

items.q: Does BioTime attendance work with my payroll?
items.a: BioTime exports attendance reports as files. Share your payroll system with AIMS to confirm the format before you order.

story.heading: Six parts at every controlled door

steps.reader: Reads a card at the door and sends it to the controller.
steps.controller: Decides who may enter, and when. InBio Pro panels run 1, 2 or 4 doors.
steps.lock: Holds the door shut with 280 kg and releases when access is granted.
steps.exit: Lets people leave from the inside without a card.
steps.card: Tap a card: the reader reads it, the controller checks it, the lock releases.
steps.software: Add users, set door hours and see every door event in one place.

items.q: Can one access panel run more than one door?
items.a: Yes. InBio Pro 160 runs one door, 260 two and 460 four. More doors take more panels.

items.q: Card, fingerprint or face for access control?
items.a: A card is the simplest. Fingerprint and face terminals check the person, not only the card. AIMS helps you choose for each door.

items.q: Can I keep my access readers?
items.a: InBio Pro panels take 26-bit Wiegand and RS485 FR series readers. Send the model and AIMS checks it.

items.q: Does the access control kit include power supplies?
items.a: The kit lists readers, the panel, locks, exit buttons and cards. An AIMS engineer confirms power supplies and cabling before quoting.

items.q: Who installs the access control kit?
items.a: An AIMS engineer confirms power supplies, cabling and door type before quoting, then installs the kit.

items.q: Tripod turnstile or swing barrier?

items.q: Who installs the turnstiles and barriers?
